rationale:
Evidence: the raced design (iteration 0, score 39.85) went off track in all 60 development trials, with 2 line-loss events per run and progress of only 0.06 to 0.17. Failure happens early, so the robot leaves the line before the bends can explain it. No race has separated overshoot, saturation or late turning, so any change is a hypothesis test.

What I kept from the critique: attribution matters more than a bundle of changes. The revision moved geometry (sensor y 0.06 to 0.04, sensor_size 0.016 to 0.012) and four controller values at once, so a result could not be traced to a cause. I also accept that the revision's kd of 0.1 is five times the raced value and that the revision's kp cut risks understeer on bends. I reject the revision as written.

What I rejected from the critique: I did not raise kp or kd, since the evidence does not show which way the controller is wrong. I did not move the sensors either. The critique's baseline is slightly off: the raced design had base 1.6 and ki 0.1, not base 1.7 and ki 0 (those were the iteration 0 proposal values, not the raced ones). I use the raced values as the reference.

What I changed: one variable only, base_speed 1.6 to 1.4, as my earlier fallback rule set. Geometry, kp, ki, kd and line_loss are exactly as raced. Reducing speed lowers lateral dynamics and saturation on the outer wheel at each bend, so it is the most direct test of whether early drift is speed-driven. The cost is time: 1.4 may not reach the 1.5 m/s needed to finish in 3 s, so completion may not occur. Survival to high progress is worth more than a time term I cannot yet meet.

Falsifiable expectations: line_loss_events fall from 2 toward 0 or 1, and max_error stays below 0.06 on the oval. If line losses still occur at 2 with the same max_error, speed is not the cause, and the next change should be kp or sensor placement, not further speed cuts. If the robot survives with progress above 0.9 but no completion, the next step is a small speed rise to about 1.5, not a controller rewrite. Geometry stays fixed so each race can be attributed to the single change.
